previous_statement: Since v and g preserve the involution, g_n(Y^dagger,X^dagger)^dagger=g_n(X,Y), and the definition w_doubleprime(X)=w_prime(X^dagger)^dagger gives the same C_0 estimate for F_(w_doubleprime). Linearity of F in its subscript gives it for w. Finally the exact bilinear expansion G_(v+w)=g-F_w-w(X)w(Y), together with ||w_n||<=2d and the product bound, gives ||G_(v^+)_n(X,Y)||<=(C_0+5)(d^2+epsilon)||X||||Y||. Thus C_m=C_0+5 is universal.
new_statement: Because v preserves the involution, g_n(Y^dagger,X^dagger)^dagger=g_n(X,Y); the definition w_doubleprime(X)=w_prime(X^dagger)^dagger therefore gives ||F_(w_doubleprime)-g_n||<=100(d^2+epsilon). Linearity of F gives the same estimate for w. The exact bilinear expansion G_(v+w)=g-F_w-w(X)w(Y), together with ||w_n||<=2d and the product bound, gives ||G_(v^+)_n(X,Y)||<=105(d^2+epsilon)||X||||Y||. Thus C_m=105 is universal.
